name: JANUS INTERNATIONAL GROUP

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: That this is a cyclical trough being mistaken for a secular decline, which is the single most common way a screen like this throws away a real opportunity. Self-storage new construction is one of the most rate-sensitive end markets in building products; it did not disappear, it was deferred, and deferred construction returns. Janus is not a distressed issuer while it waits: it generated $55.0M of free cash flow in a bad first half, its trailing free cash flow conversion is 129% of adjusted net income, it repriced its term loan 50bp TIGHTER in February 2026 at 5.62% with no maturity until 2030, and it is buying back stock. At $4.45 the equity is $607M against a business still converting north of $100M a year. The market requiring a 6-8% annual DECLINE for five consecutive years is a bet that nothing ever recovers, and the engine's flag - possible_trough_cycle_base at 0.58x - is pointing at something real even if its arithmetic is wrong.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: Self-storage REIT 2027 development guidance (Public Storage, Extra Space, CubeSmart capital plans), and Janus's own New Construction order book and backlog commentary at Q3 2026 - specifically whether New Construction growth, currently +20.3%, is being sustained organically once Kiwi II laps.
devils_advocate.already_visible: Enough to stop me calling this cheap, but not enough to dismiss the counter, which is why this lands at no_edge rather than a verdict in either direction. Supporting the counter: New Construction revenue is genuinely growing 20.3% and R3 6.6%, so the self-storage side is not collapsing - the 21.2% decline is Commercial, a different end market. Against it: the margin evidence is the problem. Revenue is guided UP 5.7% while adjusted EBITDA is guided DOWN 4.9%, which means Janus is buying revenue through Kiwi II at margins well below its own, and the incremental business is dilutive. That is the EFOR pattern - flat-to-growing headline revenue purchased with acquisition cash that CFO-less-capex never charges for - and it means the organic business is worse than the headline. On the corrected base the market requires -6% to -8%, not the -15.8% the screen reported, so the counter's strongest quantitative claim (that the market demands an absurd decline) mostly dissolves once the base is right.
devils_advocate.unresolved: Whether the 129% free cash flow conversion is sustainable or is working capital releasing as volumes fall - a shrinking manufacturer liquidates inventory and receivables, which flatters cash conversion exactly when earnings deteriorate, and I could not separate the two from the disclosure available.

what_changed: Q2 2026 (2026-08-11): revenue $233.5M, up 2.4%, below expectations; shares fell 14%. Total Self-Storage revenues +15.4% (New Construction +20.3%, R3 +6.6%) but Commercial and Other -21.2%. Full-year guidance CUT to revenue $925-945M and adjusted EBITDA $150-170M, with management now expecting North America ORGANIC self-storage revenues to decline high single digits in 2026 and citing project delays and extended timelines at Kiwi II. Six-month operating cash flow $60.6M and free cash flow $55.0M; trailing-twelve-month free cash flow conversion of adjusted net income 129%. Surpassed 500,000 installed Noke units. Repurchased ~367,000 shares for $1.9M. On 2026-02-02 the First Lien Term Loan was repriced 50bp tighter (Amendment No. 8); the rate at 2026-07-04 was 5.62%, maturity 2030.
consensus_case: At $4.45, down 57% over twelve months, the market is pricing Janus as a business whose end market has structurally reset rather than cyclically dipped. North American self-storage new construction tripled through 2021-2023 when street rates and cap rates made development trivially financeable; that condition has reversed, and the self-storage REITs have cut development pipelines. Janus's own guidance concedes the point: full-year 2026 revenue of $925-945M is up 5.7% at the midpoint while adjusted EBITDA of $150-170M is DOWN 4.9%, and the revenue growth is entirely acquired - Kiwi II Construction contributed $19.2M in the second quarter alone. Strip that out and organic revenue is falling. The market's implied decline is therefore not an overreaction; it is an extrapolation of a margin structure that has gone from roughly 28% adjusted EBITDA margin at the 2023 peak to a guided 17.1%.
base_case_rationale: The engine's $193.0M base cannot be right: it exceeds the company's own guided full-year adjusted EBITDA midpoint of $160M, which is arithmetically impossible for a business that also pays cash interest, cash taxes and capex. Rebuilding it from the guidance - first-half free cash flow of $55.0M with a stronger declared second half gives roughly $110-120M for the year, plus after-tax interest of about $23M - puts the true base near $138M, some 40% below the engine's. On growth, I underwrite -5%: Commercial is shrinking at a 21% rate and organic self-storage at high single digits, against which R3 retrofit (counter-cyclical, since it monetises existing facilities rather than new ones) and the 500,000-unit Noke installed base provide a partial and slow offset. I do not underwrite a return to 2023 volumes inside five years, because the rate environment that produced them has not returned and the REIT development pipelines are the binding constraint.
key_risks: Gross leverage of roughly 3.4x ($538.9M term debt against $150-170M guided adjusted EBITDA) into a declining EBITDA base
Adjusted EBITDA margin compression from ~28% at the 2023 peak to 17.1% guided, with no demonstrated floor
Revenue growth is entirely acquired (Kiwi II) and the acquisition is already reporting project delays and extended timelines
Commercial and Other declining 21.2% with no stated stabilisation plan
Free cash flow conversion of 129% may be working-capital release rather than earnings quality
watch_for: Self-storage REIT 2027 development capital plans - the actual driver of New Construction
Organic New Construction growth once Kiwi II laps in 2027
Whether Noke's 500,000 installed units begin producing disclosed recurring revenue
